column1: # arm-poses.csv - named whole-arm poses for the Emre Kalem arm
# WHAT THIS FILE IS. joint-limits.csv says how far each joint MAY go. This file
# says where the arm should BE for a named purpose - storage- pick-approach- and
# so on. Every row here was driven on the real arm and photographed- not planned
# on paper.
# WHY THE ENTRY PATH IS A COLUMN AND NOT A COMMENT. The endpoint is not enough.
# Two poses can both be safe while the straight line between them drives the claw
# through the bench- the wire loom- or the base housing. entry_path records the
# waypoint sequence that was actually driven and observed to be clear- joint by
# joint- in order. TO LEAVE A POSE- REVERSE ITS OWN ENTRY PATH. Do not
# interpolate between two poses in this file and assume the middle is clear.
# NO POSE HERE IS SELF-SUPPORTING. Every one is held by servo torque alone. The
# instant the holder daemon stops or the rocker goes off- all five live joints
# detach together and the arm falls from wherever it is. A pose can only be
# chosen to make that fall SHORT and to keep it away from the loom and the bench
# edge - it can never prevent it. Support the forearm by hand before switching
# off. See .claude/skills/arm-bench-safety/SKILL.md.
# J0 IS ABSENT FROM EVERY ROW ON PURPOSE. Its servo is dead and the joint is
# deliberately left detached- so no pose commands it. Its replacement was ordered
# 2026-08-06 and J0 must be re-measured when fitted - a new horn seats on a
# different spline tooth- so the old 29-110 will not point where it used to.
# J6 ANGLES ARE COMMANDED- NOT ACTUAL. As of 2026-08-06 evening the gripper does
# not articulate: the firmware ramps D11 correctly and the fingers do not move.
# Operator's diagnosis after checking it by hand - the gear is slipping on the
# motor shaft. Any j6_deg below is what the joint was TOLD- and should not be
# read as a finger position until the mechanical fault is fixed and re-verified.
# ANGLES ARE COMMANDED SOFT-LIMIT DEGREES- the same units as joint-limits.csv.
# Nothing in this system observes an output shaft- so "verified" in this file
# means a camera confirmed the arm MOVED and reached a photographed pose - never
# that a shaft is at a measured angle. The camera is uncalibrated
# is derived from pixels.
# DIRECTION MAPPING - HARD-WON- AND ONE OF THEM I GOT BACKWARDS FIRST
#   J1 shoulder  HIGHER = folds over ONTO THE BASE.  LOWER = reaches OUT.
#                Read from pixel height alone this looks inverted- because the
#                claw RISES in frame as the arm folds onto the base. A flat
#                camera projection cannot tell rising from folding. The operator
#                called it correctly from the 3D geometry and the projection did
#                not. When the two disagree- the operator wins.
#   J3 elbow     HIGHER = folded and tucked in.  LOWER = extended out.
#                Re-test this after any large J1 change: with the shoulder laid
#                over- the frame of reference has rotated ~87 degrees and the
#                screen direction of an elbow move is not what it was.
# Do not put a comma inside any field. Use a semicolon or a dash.
pose_name,j1_deg,j3_deg,j4_deg,j5_deg,j6_deg,camera_verified,date_recorded,entry_path,notes

storage,88,64,90,104,70,yes,2026-08-06,J1 1>22>34>46>58>70>80>88 at 5 deg/s then J3 52>60>64 at 20 deg/s,THE PARKING POSE. Shoulder folded over onto the base and elbow tucked- so the arm is collapsed against its own base rather than reaching out over the bench. Stopped deliberately 3 degrees short of J1 max 91 and 2 short of J3 max 66 - a joint parked hard against its own soft limit has nowhere to back off to and that is the mistake that cost J0 an afternoon. Driven in 8-12 degree steps with a camera frame after every step
column2: every waypoint parked at the commanded angle with CL=0 and JTO=0- and the session logged ZERO watchdog latches. Wrist left at its home 90/104 untouched on purpose: J4's travel ends are still UNCONFIRMED - 0-180 is the whole electrical range - and the claw was inches off the bench during the fold- so driving the wrist blind is how the claw gets pushed into the mat. ON POWER-OFF the forearm swings down through the base area where the wire loom and the blue cable sit
column3: hand under the forearm BEFORE the rocker. Evidence: Calibration_Notes/evidence/2026-08-06_motion-verify/

column1: pick_approach,26,18,140,165,70,yes,2026-08-06,from storage: J3 64>56 then J1 88>76>64>52>40>28>16 at 5 deg/s then J1 16>26 then J3 56>18 then J5 104>165 then J4 90>140,POISED ABOVE THE TABLE - FOREARM LEVEL AND CLAW POINTING STRAIGHT DOWN. Revision of the first attempt (J3 64 / J5 130) after the operator said the elbow section should be basically horizontal and the gripper should point down more. WHAT SETS WHAT - three independent things and it is worth knowing which knob does which: J3 sets the FOREARM ANGLE (64 slopes it steeply down
column4: 18 is level - confirmed against a drawn horizontal reference). J5 ROLL swings the claw about the forearm axis (60 and 90 point the prongs UP
column6: 165 hangs them down). J4 PITCH then fine-aims it (110 leaves ~35 deg off vertical
column8: 170 swings past). PITCH ALONE CANNOT AIM THE CLAW - roll has to put the pitch axis in a useful plane first- which is why the first attempt needed three tries to measure. LOWERING THIS POSE WHILE KEEPING THE FOREARM LEVEL IS NEARLY OUT OF ROOM: higher J3 tilts the forearm DOWN- so dropping J1 must be matched by dropping J3 too- and J3 is already at 18 of a 0 floor. Roughly J1 14 / J3 6 is the lowest level-forearm reach available- and J3 6 sits close to its soft limit. Compensating the WRONG way (J1 down + J3 up) retracts the arm upward instead - that was tested and photographed. J4=140 and J5=165 are both further out than this arm had been driven before: J4 had only seen 75-105 and J5 only 60-150. Both reached with CL=0 JTO=0 and no stall. J5 165 leaves 13 deg to its 178 max- and that 178 may be electrical rather than mechanical- so do not push it. J6 commanded open at 70 but the gripper does not articulate. Evidence: Calibration_Notes/evidence/2026-08-06_motion-verify/
